results.title: US Section 301 Tariffs on Chinese EVs and Batteries ...
results.content:
The US Section 301 tariff regime on Chinese EVs and batteries, as of August 2026, represents a structural barrier of unprecedented magnitude, imposing a 100% ad valorem duty on Chinese EV imports and a 25% tariff on lithium-ion battery cells and packs, alongside a 7.5% tariff on graphite and critical minerals. This policy is not merely a trade measure but a strategic instrument designed to decouple the US energy storage supply chain from Chinese dominance. The effective exclusion of Chinese EVs [...] The 100% tariff applies to Chinese-made electric vehicles (HS 8703.80) and certain other EV categories, including buses and trucks. The 25% tariff applies to lithium-ion battery cells (HS 8507.60) and battery packs, as well as certain battery components. The 7.5% tariff applies to natural graphite (HS 2504.10) and critical minerals (e.g., cobalt, nickel, lithium) used in battery production. It's important to note that the tariffs are ad valorem, meaning they are calculated on the customs value [...] As of August 2026, the US Section 301 tariffs on Chinese EVs remain at 100%, effectively blocking direct imports. Battery tariffs are 25% on lithium-ion cells and packs, with a 7.5% tariff on graphite and critical minerals. These measures have accelerated reshoring and nearshoring, with US battery manufacturing capacity projected to reach 1,200 GWh by 2026, but costs remain 20-30% higher than Chinese equivalents.
